claims.text: Local composition fluctuations in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles create nanoscale regions enriched in lower-melting constituents.
Lower-melting enriched regions act as hotspots for premelting and govern the onset and progression of melting.
The homogeneous and heterogeneous comparison groups can be prepared with identical nominally equimolar global compositions.
Processing can intentionally introduce controlled local compositional inhomogeneities while retaining the same global composition.
STEM-EDS can characterize elemental distributions and local chemistry.
Regions exhibiting elemental segregation or clustering have a lower local melting point than the surrounding uniform matrix.
Regions enriched in elements with lower intrinsic melting temperatures become thermally activated at lower temperatures.
Thermal activation of lower-melting enriched regions initiates localized premelting.
Localized premelting propagates through an inhomogeneous nanoparticle, causing overall transformation below the temperature observed in a homogeneous nanoparticle.
Nanoparticles with intentionally induced composition fluctuations will exhibit earlier and more spatially localized premelting than homogeneous nanoparticles.
Detectably segregated regions will begin melting before other regions of the same nanoparticle.
Uniformly mixed nanoparticles will lack a spatial correlation between elemental segregation and melting initiation.
FMBP can produce HEA nanoparticles in which constituent elements are uniformly mixed without phase separation.
Compositionally uniform HEA nanoparticles have a more uniform and higher melting-onset temperature than compositionally inhomogeneous HEA nanoparticles.
The proposed mechanism should hold from a few nanometers to tens of nanometers for equimolar or near-equimolar multielement nanoparticles.
Strong nanoparticle-substrate interactions can modify or dominate thermal behavior.
Surface strain may modify or dominate HEA nanoparticle melting behavior.

Similar premelting-onset temperatures in the two groups together with no statistically significant spatial correlation between heterogeneity and melting initiation would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
